evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: `manager_restarted` proves only that the manager PID and invocation ID are nonempty and differ. A guest reboot changes both, so it can satisfy this check. The separate `boot_id_changed` check only proves the reboot phase saw a boot change; it does not constrain the manager before/after snapshots to the same boot. Requiring nonempty equal guest boot IDs across the manager restart is a routine tightening of the existing proof, not a new requirement or contract conflict.
